newsitem.title: DUBAI: Kidnapped U.S. engineer released in Yemen-embassy.
newsitem.headline: Kidnapped U.S. engineer released in Yemen-embassy.

text.p: An American oil engineer kidnapped by a Yemeni mountain tribe has been released from 16 days in captivity, a U.S. embassy spokesman said on Thursday.
"I can confirm he was released last night," the spokesman said by telephone from Sanaa. He would not give other details.

Joe D'ellaire, an engineer working for the U.S. engineering group Halliburton was abducted on February 10 in Yemen's eastern Marib governorate by members of the Murad tribe who were angered by a land dispute with Yemeni officials.
It was not immediatedly clear whether any of the captors' demands had been met in return for D'ellaire's release.
Yemeni security sources had said the captors were demanding compensation of $2 million or the return of a piece of land in Sanaa they say was given to one of their tribal leaders.

In recent years, Yemeni tribes with grievances against the government or foreign oil companies have kidnapped scores of tourists, diplomats or other foreigners to use as bargaining chips. The hostages were all released unharmed.
